scenes.narration: ChatGPT has never read a single word you typed.
Welcome to FredsDesk, lesson four. In under a minute, you'll see exactly what AI reads instead.
It reads tokens. A token is a small chunk of text that a model reads as one piece.
scenes.definition: A small chunk of text that an AI model reads as one piece.

scenes.narration: Think of LEGO. The model can't swallow a whole sentence at once, so your text gets snapped into bricks, and every brick is one token.
Watch this sentence split. Common words stay whole, but long or rare words, like unbelievable, break into smaller parts. Then each piece becomes a number, because computers only understand numbers.
That's why AI can struggle to count the R's in strawberry. It never sees letters. It only sees tokens.
scenes.question: How many R's?

scenes.narration: Quick recap. One: AI reads tokens, not letters. Two: long or rare words split into pieces. Three: a token is about three quarters of a word.
points: Long or rare words split into pieces
